correctness.rationale: The second-iterate difference property follows from the floor of a contraction over adjacent integers; the displacement is nonincreasing by unit decrements. Bounded rounding defects force a zero interval, strictly monotone integer sequences prove endpoint capture without overshoot, and \(f^2=\mathrm{id}\) on the core implies reversal. Exact half-open cells solve all real basin boundary cases; \(g^k(n)=r^{2k}n+O(1)\) uniformly in k proves the logarithmic first-entry time with parameter-dependent \(O(1)\). The full proof is in RESULT.md and finite corroboration in CHECK.py.
